facts.text: Vassar’s roots trace back to 1887 when a post office moved from the extinct La Mont’s Hill and was renamed Vassar, officially establishing the town.
The Missouri Pacific Railroad once ran through Vassar, but after abandonment it was transformed into the scenic Flint Hills Nature Trail.
In 1969, Bruce and Veda Rogers, with Veda’s brother Richard Driver and his wife Ruth, converted an old barn into the Vassar Playhouse, a theater that strengthened culture.
Vassar sits just half a mile south of Pomona Lake, making it a popular spot for boating, fishing, and camping.
Every October, Vassar hosts a fall festival featuring live music, crafts, games, food, a parade, costume contest, auction, and pie contest.
The Vassar Playhouse opened in 1969, turning an old barn into a summer theater that became a cultural hub for the community.
